title_en: Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Further Deepening the Reform of Diversified Dispute Resolution Mechanisms by People's Courts
keywords_en: Arbitration; Courts further deepening diversified dispute resolution
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Deepening the Reform of the Diversified Dispute Resolution Mechanism by the People's Courts

Fa Fa [2016] No. 14

Deeply advancing the reform of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism is an important measure for the people's courts to deepen judicial reform and achieve judicial fairness for the people; it is an important element of modernizing the national governance system and governance capacity; and it is an inevitable requirement for promoting social fairness and justice and maintaining social harmony and stability. To implement the "Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Several Major Issues Concerning Comprehensively Advancing the Rule of Law" and the "Opinions on Improving the Diversified Mechanism for Resolving Conflicts and Disputes" issued by the General Office of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the General Office of the State Council, the following opinions are put forward for the people's courts to further deepen the reform of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism and improve the dispute resolution mechanism that links litigation with non-litigation.

I. Guiding Ideology, Main Objectives, and Basic Principles

1. Guiding ideology. Fully implement the spirit of the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and the Third, Fourth, and Fifth Plenary Sessions of the 18th Central Committee, take Deng Xiaoping Theory, the important thought of the "Three Represents," and the Scientific Outlook on Development as guidance, deeply implement the spirit of General Secretary Xi Jinping's series of important speeches, closely focus on the coordinated promotion of the "Four Comprehensives" strategic layout and the five development concepts, actively adapt to the new normal of economic development, take institutional and mechanism innovation as the driving force, effectively resolve various disputes, continuously meet the diverse judicial needs of the people, and ensure that the people live and work in peace and contentment and that society is stable and orderly.

2. Main objectives. In accordance with the working idea of "the state formulating development strategies, the judiciary playing a guiding role, and promoting the national legislative process," build a litigation-mediation connection platform with complete functions, diverse forms, and standardized operation, smooth the channels for dispute resolution, and guide the parties to choose appropriate dispute resolution methods; rationally allocate social resources for dispute resolution, improve a diversified dispute resolution mechanism with organic linkage and mutual coordination among reconciliation, mediation, arbitration, notarization, administrative adjudication, administrative reconsideration, and litigation; fully play the guiding, driving, and guaranteeing role of the judiciary in the construction of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism, and provide strong judicial guarantees for promoting sustained and healthy economic and social development and building a moderately prosperous society in all respects.

3. Basic principles.

-- Adhere to the leadership of the Party and government, coordination of comprehensive management, and multi-party co-governance, and build a working pattern in which various forces participate together in dispute resolution.

-- Adhere to judicial guidance, litigation-mediation connection, and social coordination, and form a joint force for dispute resolution with multi-level and multi-field participation from all sectors of society.

-- Adhere to optimizing resources, improving systems, and ensuring the rule of law, and enhance the legal effect of social organizations in resolving disputes.

-- Adhere to a people-oriented approach, voluntariness and legality, and convenience for the people, and establish an efficient and convenient litigation service and dispute resolution mechanism.

-- Adhere to basing on national conditions, reasonable reference, reform and innovation, and improve a diversified dispute resolution system with Chinese characteristics.

II. Strengthening Platform Construction

4. Improving platform settings. People's courts at all levels should integrate the construction of litigation-mediation connection platforms with the construction of litigation service centers, and establish a comprehensive service platform integrating multiple functions such as litigation services, case registration, litigation-mediation connection, and petition-related litigation. People's courts should be equipped with specialized personnel to engage in litigation-mediation connection work, establish a long-term working mechanism for litigation-mediation connection, and, based on the types of cases accepted in their jurisdiction, introduce relevant mediation, arbitration, notarization, and other institutions or organizations to set up mediation studios and service windows in litigation service centers and other departments. They may also dispatch personnel to guide litigation-mediation connection work in areas with frequent disputes and at the grassroots level (townships, subdistricts, villages, communities).

5. Clarifying platform responsibilities. The litigation-mediation connection platform of the people's courts is responsible for the following work: appropriately diverting disputes brought to the court, guiding parties to choose non-litigation methods to resolve disputes suitable for mediation; conducting assigned mediation and entrusted mediation; handling judicial confirmation cases; managing the rosters of specially invited mediation organizations and specially invited mediators; strengthening guidance on mediation work, promoting the organic connection between litigation and non-litigation dispute resolution methods in terms of procedural arrangements, validity confirmation, and legal guidance; and perfecting the joint working system of people's mediation, administrative mediation, commercial mediation, industry mediation, and judicial mediation.

6. Strengthening connection with comprehensive management organizations. People's courts may rely on the comprehensive social security management platform to establish a connection mechanism for the investigation and resolution of conflicts and disputes; for group disputes and major cases, promptly report and provide feedback and carry out emergency handling, and establish regular or irregular joint meeting systems to form an interactive mechanism for dispute resolution with information sharing, complementary advantages, and collaborative cooperation.

7. Strengthening connection with administrative organs. People's courts should strengthen communication and coordination with administrative organs, and promote the connection between litigation and mechanisms such as administrative mediation, administrative reconsideration, and administrative adjudication. Support administrative organs in conducting mediation or adjudication upon the application of the parties or ex officio, or in making other dispositions according to law. In key areas such as public security management, social security, traffic accident compensation, medical and health care, consumer rights protection, property management, environmental pollution, intellectual property, and securities and futures, support administrative organs or administrative mediation organizations in conducting administrative reconciliation and administrative mediation according to law.

8. Strengthening connection with people's mediation organizations. Continuously improve guidance on people's mediation work, promote the institutionalization and standardization of people's mediation organizations, and further expand the scope and scale of people's mediation organizations assisting the people's courts in resolving disputes. Support the innovative development of specialized and professional people's mediation organizations in areas prone to frequent disputes, establish and improve a network of mediation organizations covering urban and rural areas, and play the fundamental role of people's mediation organizations in promptly and locally resolving civil disputes, resolving grassroots conflicts, and maintaining grassroots stability.

9. Strengthening connection with commercial mediation organizations and industry mediation organizations. Actively promote chambers of commerce, industry associations, mediation associations, private non-enterprise units, commercial arbitration institutions, and others with the appropriate conditions to establish commercial mediation organizations or industry mediation organizations, and provide commercial mediation services or industry mediation services in areas such as investment, finance, securities and futures, insurance, real estate, engineering contracting, technology transfer, environmental protection, e-commerce, intellectual property, and international trade. Improve mediation rules and connection procedures, and leverage the specialization and professionalism advantages of commercial mediation organizations and industry mediation organizations.

10. Strengthening connection with arbitration institutions. Actively support the reform of the arbitration system, and strengthen communication and connection with commercial arbitration institutions, labor and personnel dispute arbitration institutions, and rural land contract arbitration institutions. Respect the laws of commercial arbitration and arbitration rules, promptly handle preservation applications from arbitration institutions, handle cases concerning the setting aside and non-enforcement of arbitration awards in accordance with legal provisions, and standardize the judicial review procedures for foreign-related and foreign commercial arbitration awards. Support the improvement of the case-handling system for labor and personnel dispute arbitration, strengthen the effective connection between labor and personnel dispute arbitration and litigation, and explore the establishment of new rules and systems for the unification of arbitration and adjudication standards. Strengthen support and guarantees for mediation and arbitration of disputes over rural land contracting and management, achieve a reasonable connection between arbitration and litigation for agricultural-related disputes, and promptly review and enforce written awards or mediation statements issued by rural land contract arbitration institutions.

11. Strengthening connection with notarization institutions. Support notarization institutions in verifying and certifying legal acts, facts, and documents according to law; support notarization institutions in notarizing creditor's rights documents for creditor's rights and debt contracts reached between parties, as well as settlement agreements and mediation agreements with content for performance; support notarization institutions in providing notarization legal services in areas such as service of process, evidence collection, preservation, and enforcement, and in conducting notarization activities or mediation services in areas such as family affairs and commerce. Enforce notarized creditor's rights documents according to law.

12. Supporting organizations such as trade unions, women's federations, the Communist Youth League, and the Law Society to participate in dispute resolution. Support trade unions, women's federations, and the Communist Youth League in participating in the resolution of disputes such as labor disputes, marriage and family disputes, and disputes over the rights and interests of women and children. Support the Law Society in mobilizing and organizing legal scholars and legal practitioners to participate in the resolution of conflicts and disputes, and provide legal consultation services and mediation work. Support other social organizations in participating in the resolution of disputes related to their functions.

13. Leveraging the role of other social forces. Fully leverage the role of people's congress deputies, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, experts and scholars, lawyers, professional technicians, grassroots organization leaders, community workers, grid administrators, and "five old personnel" (old Party members, old cadres, old teachers, old intellectuals, old political and legal cadres) in participating in dispute resolution. Support psychological counselors, marriage and family guidance instructors, certified public accountants, college student volunteers, and others in providing services such as psychological counseling, evaluation, appraisal, and mediation to the masses. Support the improvement of the construction of public welfare and charitable social organizations and urban and rural community service organizations, and encourage their participation in dispute resolution.

14. Strengthening the construction of "one-stop" dispute resolution platforms. In areas such as road traffic, labor disputes, medical and health care, property management, consumer rights protection, land contracting, environmental protection, and other areas where disputes are frequent, people's courts may integrate resources with administrative organs, people's mediation organizations, and industry mediation organizations to promote the establishment of a "one-stop" dispute resolution service platform, effectively reducing the burden on the masses.

15. Innovating online dispute resolution methods. In accordance with the requirements of the "Internet+" strategy, promote the use of modern information technology in the diversified dispute resolution mechanism. Promote the establishment of an information platform integrating online mediation, online case registration, online judicial confirmation, online trial, electronic supervision procedures, and electronic service of process, to achieve functions such as case prediction, information sharing, resource integration, and data analysis for dispute resolution, and promote the informatization development of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism.

16. Promoting the international development of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism. Fully respect the diversity of legal cultures of Chinese and foreign parties, and support their voluntary choice of non-litigation methods such as mediation and arbitration to resolve disputes. Further strengthen exchanges and cooperation between China and other countries and regions with judicial institutions, arbitration institutions, and mediation organizations, and enhance the international competitiveness and credibility of China's dispute resolution mechanism. Leverage the advantages of various dispute resolution methods, continuously meet the diverse dispute resolution needs of Chinese and foreign parties, and provide judicial services and guarantees for the implementation of major national strategies such as the "Belt and Road" initiative.

III. Improving System Construction

17. Improving the system of specially invited mediation. People's courts may admit people's mediation, administrative mediation, commercial mediation, industry mediation, or other organizations with mediation functions as specially invited mediation organizations, and admit qualified individuals such as people's congress deputies, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, people's jurors, experts and scholars, lawyers, arbitrators, and retired legal practitioners as specially invited mediators. Clarify the scope of duties of specially invited mediation organizations or specially invited mediators, formulate provisions for specially invited mediation, improve the procedures for specially invited mediation, perfect the roster management system, and strengthen the construction of the specially invited mediation team.

18. Establishing a full-time mediator system in courts. People's courts may assign full-time mediators in litigation service centers and other departments, to be held by judges or judicial assistants skilled in mediation, responsible for mediation guidance work and entrusted mediation work after case registration. If a mediation agreement is reached under the auspices of a judge, a mediation statement shall be issued according to law; if a mediation agreement is reached under the auspices of a judicial assistant, a mediation statement shall be issued after review by a judge according to law.

19. Promoting the construction of a lawyer mediation system. People's courts should strengthen communication and connection with judicial administrative departments, bar associations, law firms, and legal aid centers, admit lawyers into the roster of specially invited mediators of the people's courts, explore the establishment of lawyer mediation studios, and encourage lawyers to participate in dispute resolution. Support lawyers in joining various mediation organizations as mediators, or in setting up lawyer mediators in law firms, to fully leverage the specialization and professionalism advantages of lawyers. Establish a recusal system for lawyers serving as mediators; a lawyer serving as a mediator shall not serve as an agent in the same case. Promote the establishment of a mechanism for lawyers to inform parties of the option to choose non-litigation methods to resolve disputes when accepting representation.

20. Improving the system of settlement and mediation in criminal proceedings. For public prosecution cases, private prosecution cases, and criminal incidental civil cases that may be settled or mediated in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, the people's court shall establish a working mechanism for connection between criminal settlement and mediation in criminal proceedings with the public security organs and procuratorial organs. It may invite grassroots organizations, specially invited mediation organizations, specially invited mediators, as well as the parties' work units or colleagues, relatives, and friends to participate in mediation, to promote the parties to reach a settlement or mediation agreement.

21. Promoting the improvement of systems such as administrative mediation, administrative reconciliation, and administrative adjudication. Support administrative organs in conducting administrative mediation in cases involving administrative compensation, compensation, and the exercise of discretionary powers by administrative organs as provided by laws and regulations; support administrative organs in guiding and promoting parties to negotiate and settle through providing factual investigation results, professional appraisals, or legal opinions; support administrative organs in adjudicating civil disputes closely related to administrative management activities according to law.

22. Exploring the neutral evaluation mechanism for civil and commercial disputes. People's courts with the appropriate conditions may explore the establishment of a neutral evaluation mechanism in areas such as medical and health care, real estate, construction engineering, intellectual property, and environmental protection, and engage experts in relevant professional fields as neutral evaluators. For civil and commercial disputes initiated by the parties, the people's court may suggest that the parties choose a neutral evaluator to assist in issuing an evaluation report, predicting the outcome of the judgment for the parties' reference. The parties may settle on their own based on the evaluation opinion, or conduct mediation through a specially invited mediator.

23. Exploring the mechanism for recording uncontested facts. When the mediation procedure concludes without the parties reaching a mediation agreement, the mediator, with the consent of all parties, may record in writing the facts that are not in dispute between the parties during the mediation process, and have the parties sign for confirmation. In the litigation procedure, unless involving national interests, social public interests, or the legitimate rights and interests of others, the parties need not provide evidence for the uncontested facts confirmed during the mediation process.

24. Exploring the mechanism for recognition of uncontested mediation proposals. If a mediation agreement cannot be reached through mediation but there is no major disagreement on the disputed facts, the mediator, with the consent of all parties, may propose a mediation proposal and serve it in writing to the parties. If the parties do not raise a written objection within seven days, the mediation proposal shall be deemed a mediation agreement voluntarily reached by the parties; if a written objection is raised, it shall be deemed that mediation has not been established. If the parties apply for judicial confirmation of the mediation agreement, it shall be confirmed in accordance with relevant provisions.

IV. Improving Procedural Arrangements

25. Establishing a dispute resolution notification procedure. The people's court shall assess the litigation risks before registration of the case, inform and guide the parties to choose appropriate non-litigation methods to resolve disputes, and provide the parties with explanations and guidance on dispute resolution methods, psychological counseling, and litigation knowledge.

26. Encouraging parties to conduct prior negotiation and settlement. Encourage parties to negotiate first to resolve disputes and reach a settlement agreement. Where both parties are represented by lawyers, encourage lawyers to guide the parties to settle first. Specially invited mediators, relevant experts, or other personnel may participate in negotiations upon the application or entrustment of the parties, providing auxiliary coordination and assistance for dispute resolution.

27. Exploring the establishment of a pre-mediation procedure. Explore the scope of disputes and types of cases for which a pre-mediation procedure may be applied. For disputes suitable for mediation, such as family disputes, neighbor relations, small-amount debts, consumer rights protection, traffic accidents, medical disputes, and property management, grassroots people's courts with the appropriate conditions shall, on the basis of soliciting the parties' willingness, guide the parties to conduct prior mediation by specially invited mediation organizations or specially invited mediators before registration of the case.

28. Perfecting the procedures for assigned and entrusted mediation. For cases suitable for mediation that are brought to the people's court by the parties, before registration of the case, the people's court may assign specially invited mediation organizations or specially invited mediators to conduct mediation. If an agreement is reached through assigned mediation, the parties may apply for judicial confirmation according to law. If the parties explicitly refuse mediation, the people's court shall register the case according to law. After registration of the case or during the trial, if the people's court considers a case suitable for mediation, with the consent of the parties, it may entrust the case to a specially invited mediation organization, a specially invited mediator, or a full-time mediator of the people's court for mediation. If an agreement is reached through entrusted mediation, a mediation statement shall be issued after review by a judge according to law.

29. Perfecting the mechanism for separating complex and simple cases. For civil and commercial cases that cannot be mediated, apply the separation of complex and simple cases, and divert cases through summary procedures, small-claims procedures, supervision procedures, and expedited adjudication mechanisms, to achieve quick trial of simple cases and refined trial of complex cases. Improve the system of leniency for admissions of guilt and acceptance of punishment, further explore the reform of expedited procedures for criminal cases, simplify work processes, and build a multi-level litigation system supporting ordinary procedures, summary procedures, and expedited procedures. In accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law, improve the mechanism for separating complex and simple administrative cases.

30. Promoting appropriate separation of mediation and adjudication. Establish a mechanism for appropriate separation of personnel and procedures for case mediation and adjudication. Judges engaged in mediation at the case filing stage shall, in principle, not participate in the adjudication of the same case. During the trial of a case, if both parties still have the willingness to mediate, the judge engaged in adjudication may conduct mediation.

31. Perfecting the judicial confirmation procedure. For agreements with the nature of civil contracts reached through mediation by administrative organs, people's mediation organizations, commercial mediation organizations, industry mediation organizations, or other organizations with mediation functions, the parties may apply to the basic people's court or people's tribunal at the location of the mediation organization for confirmation of their validity according to law. For agreements reached through mediation by specially invited mediation organizations or specially invited mediators assigned before registration of the case, if the parties apply for judicial confirmation, it shall be under the jurisdiction of the basic people's court at the location of the mediation organization or the court that assigned the mediation.

32. Strengthening the connection between mediation and supervision procedures. For settlement agreements and mediation agreements with content for the payment of money or negotiable securities, if the creditor applies to the basic people's court with jurisdiction for a payment order in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and its judicial interpretations, the people's court shall issue a payment order according to law. If the debtor fails to raise a written objection within the statutory period and fails to perform the payment order after the period expires, the people's court may enforce it compulsorily.

V. Strengthening Work Guarantees

33. Strengthening organizational leadership. People's courts at all levels should further strengthen organizational leadership over litigation-mediation connection work, and establish a working mechanism with overall coordination, clear division of labor, and individual responsibility. They should actively seek support from the Party committee, the People's Congress, and the government, promote the issuance of local supporting documents for the construction of a diversified dispute resolution mechanism, and promote the construction of a scientific and systematic diversified dispute resolution system.

34. Strengthening guidance and supervision. Higher-level people's courts should effectively strengthen guidance and supervision over lower-level people's courts, and promptly summarize experiences that can be replicated and promoted in the reform of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism. Higher people's courts should designate specialized institutions, formulate implementation plans, grasp the work situation, and actively carry out the selection of model courts for the reform of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism within their jurisdiction. Intermediate people's courts should strengthen guidance and supervision over grassroots people's courts within their jurisdiction, and promote continuous and effective results in the reform of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism.

35. Improving the management mechanism. Establish a case management system for litigation-mediation connection, and include the content of assigned mediation, entrusted mediation, full-time mediation, and judicial confirmation into the case management system and judicial statistics system. Improve the management system for specially invited mediation organizations, specially invited mediators, and full-time mediators of the court, and establish reward and punishment mechanisms.

36. Strengthen Training of Mediation Personnel. Improve the training mechanism for specially invited mediators and full-time mediators, and cooperate with relevant departments to promote the establishment of a professional and occupational mediator qualification certification system, strengthen professional ethics, and jointly improve the evaluation system for the professional competence of mediators.

37. Strengthen Funding Guarantees. People's courts at all levels shall actively seek support from Party committees and governments, include dispute resolution expenses in special fiscal budgets, and actively explore entrusting dispute resolution to social forces through methods such as purchasing services. Support commercial mediation organizations, industry mediation organizations, law firms, etc., to operate in accordance with market principles, providing dispute resolution services based on the needs of the parties and charging appropriate fees.

38. Leverage the Role of Litigation Costs as a Lever. Where the parties reach a settlement on their own and apply for withdrawal of the lawsuit, the case acceptance fee shall be exempted. Where the parties accept court-entrusted mediation, the people's court may appropriately reduce the litigation costs. Where one party, without正当 reason, fails to participate in mediation or fails to perform the mediation agreement, or intentionally delays the litigation, the people's court may, at its discretion, increase that party's share of the litigation costs.

39. Strengthen Publicity and Theoretical Research. People's courts at all levels shall vigorously publicize the advantages of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism, encourage and guide parties to prioritize non-litigation methods that are lower in cost, less adversarial, and conducive to repairing relationships for resolving disputes. Establish a modern dispute resolution concept of "state leadership, judicial promotion, social participation, diversity of means, and rule of law guarantee," and create a social atmosphere of integrity and friendliness, rationality and peace, civility and harmony, and innovation and development. Strengthen exchange and cooperation with political and legal universities, research institutions, and other entities, actively promote the transformation of research results, and fully leverage the guiding role of diversified dispute resolution theory in judicial practice. Draw on extraterritorial experience to conduct in-depth research on the functional role of people's courts in the diversified dispute resolution mechanism.

40. Promote the Legislative Process. People's courts shall promptly summarize the successful experiences of local diversified dispute resolution mechanism reforms, actively support the enactment of relevant local regulations and local government rules tailored to local conditions within their jurisdictions, thereby advancing the legislative process for relevant laws at the national level, institutionalizing and legalizing the achievements of reform practices, and promoting the healthy development of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism reform within the track of the rule of law.

June 28, 2016
